label: conj:gs-residue-at-root-existence
title: Existence of the cyclotomic residue at each filtration level
html:
Conjecture. Existence of the cyclotomic residue at each filtration level

Conjecture (cyclotomic residue exists at each level). For each filtration level \ell \in \{0, 1, \ldots, \ell(K, q)\} and each primitive \ell-th root of unity \zeta_\ell, the cyclotomic projection

  \mathrm{Res}_{q \to \zeta_\ell}\bigl[\Phi_q(u) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w)\bigr] \;\in\; \mathbb{R}

is a well-defined real number. Here \Phi_q is the quantum dilogarithm. The value depends only on \ell and the equivalence class of T_w modulo J^{\ell+1}(q).

Categorical statement. The cyclotomic projection of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M,\ell} in the Habiro completion forms the residue contribution attached to stratum \ell by the filtered Hochschild spectral sequence.

Lean encoding. The conjecture is axiomatised as the class QOU.BraidKnot.ResidueAtRoot (fields: the target ring family target : ℕ → Type and the cyclotomic projection project : (n : ℕ) → R →+* target n); an instance supplies the Habiro-completion projection whose existence is the conjectural content, and prop:residue-at-root is stated conditionally on it per the conditional-class convention. The archimedean per-level residue values enter downstream as the class field residue : Fin levelBound → ℝ of GBResidueSpectralSum. A fully constructive definition requires Mathlib infrastructure for meromorphic functions and the Habiro completion as a topological ring.

Conjectural status. The analytic literature guarantees the existence and reality of the residue. A Lean proof awaits the meromorphic-function infrastructure. Instances supply the value directly.

Empirical witness. The canonical residues for the proton, neutron, and deuteron at q_0 match the Habiro side at machine precision.
